divergence: Arity, walk depth, scope and trigger class all diverge; the key NAME is right. (1) Type is `string`, not `string[]` — `storage.ts:273-276` silently turns an array into `''`, so a doc-shaped `["a","b"]` disables fallback rather than configuring it. (2) Exactly one hop: the `fallbackModelRetry` guard at `pi-agent.ts:6314` makes entries two and three unreachable even if they existed; no dedup, no three-entry cap, no `"default"` expansion, no `availableModels` drop. (3) The switch is permanent, not per-turn — `pi-agent.ts:6335` never restores the primary and pushes `set_model` to the subprocess, contradicting `model-config.md:365`. (4) Trigger class is wrong in both directions against `model-config.md:363`: we DO fall back on `network_error` (a transport error the page excludes) and on `invalid_model`/`model_no_tool_support` (config errors, not "overloaded, unavailable, or another non-retryable server error"), while we never see rate-limit/billing separately because they are simply absent from the set. (5) Compaction is not covered at all (`pi-agent.ts:5596-5599`), so the smaller-context-window rule has nowhere to live. (6) The whole mechanism is Pi-only; Claude sessions have none. (7) The sentence's second clause — `--fallback-model` applying to interactive sessions — has no counterpart: `apps/cli` has no such flag. (8) Even the single hop is unreachable for a user in a packaged build: the only surface for the key is a file `syncConfigDefaults` overwrites each launch.

change.what: Widen to `fallbackModel: string | string[]` (accept the legacy scalar on read forever — this key is on disk in every existing install) and rewrite the docstring: an ordered chain of Pi model IDs, deduped, capped at three, tried in order for the current turn only.

Replace the string-only coercion with a normalizer that accepts a string, a comma-separated string and an array: trim each entry, drop empties, dedupe preserving first occurrence, cap at three, and expose the result as `string[]` (`[]` = disabled). Keep `FALLBACK_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.workspaceDefaults.fallbackModel` writing a value the widened type accepts. This is a persisted-shape change — the read path must never throw on the old scalar.
`z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])`. One line. Note this schema is test-only today, so it proves nothing at runtime — the load-path normalizer in storage.ts is the real gate.

Add `normalizePiFallbackModelChain(raw: unknown, opts: { defaultModelId?: string; isAllowed?: (id: string) => boolean }): string[]` beside it — split on commas, trim, expand the literal `"default"` to `opts.defaultModelId`, drop entries `opts.isAllowed` rejects (wire `isManagedModelAllowed` from `config/managed-models.ts` here; it is a pure predicate, so this stays on the READ side and does not touch the persistence boundary that module's header forbids), dedupe, then slice to 3. Keep the scalar helper as a thin wrapper so existing callers compile.

Turn the one-shot into a walk: replace `PiChatOptions.fallbackModelRetry?: boolean` with `fallbackChainIndex?: number`; `getFallbackModel` returns `string[]` via the new chain normalizer; `getRetryFallbackModel` picks the entry at `(options?.fallbackChainIndex ?? -1) + 1`, skipping any entry equal to the primary, and returns null once the chain is exhausted; `retryWithFallbackModel` records the primary model once, calls `setModel(next)`, keeps the existing `info` notice, and passes `fallbackChainIndex` forward. Restore the primary in `chatImpl`'s `finally` (:6808, next to the `ownsModelTurnBudget` release) so the switch lasts the current turn only — the same `setModel` path already re-forwards `set_model` to the subprocess. Also drop `network_error` from `FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES` (`model-config.md:363` excludes transport errors) and decide explicitly, in a comment, whether `invalid_model`/`model_no_tool_support` stay — they are not the documented trigger class, but a retired pinned model is exactly the `:385` case, so keeping them is defensible if written down.

blastRadius: Crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary and therefore trips this repo's risk trigger: `fallbackModel` lives in `~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json`, written from `apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json` by `syncConfigDefaults` (`storage.ts:200-227`) and read by `loadConfigDefaults` (`storage.ts:233-281`), which is called on every Pi turn through `getFallbackModel`. Widening `string` → `string | string[]` changes `ConfigDefaults` in `config-defaults-schema.ts`, a type re-exported from the shared package, so every reader of `workspaceDefaults` typechecks against it. Readers/tests to update: `packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/validators-stored-config.test.ts:127,165-166,179,189,195,200-207` (four cases pass `fallbackModel` as a bare string), `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-fallback-model.test.ts` (stubs `getFallbackModel` at :76 and asserts the persistent switch at :99), `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-max-turns.test.ts:264-265` (stubs `getRetryFallbackModel` with the `fallbackModelRetry` option shape — renaming the option breaks it). The turn-scoped restore touches `setModel` (`pi-agent.ts:6980-6992`), which emits a `ConfigChange` automation hook and sends `set_model` over the Pi subprocess JSONL wire (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:2411,4022,4097` are the receiving side), so a restore doubles the `ConfigChange` events per fallback turn — anything matching on `config_keys: ['model']` sees the extra event. `SessionManager.ts:14716-14717` is the other `setModel` caller (user-driven model change through `withPinnedConfigChange`); a mid-turn user switch racing the restore needs a decision. Wiring `isManagedModelAllowed` in pulls `config/managed-models.ts` / `agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts` into the chain read — read-only use of a pure predicate, but that module's header forbids handing any filtered result to a writer, so the chain must never be written back. `apps/electron/dist/resources/config-defaults.json:28` is a build output carrying the same value and will regenerate. No imported-plugin path reads this key.
userImpact: Latent for almost every user, because the key is unreachable: the shipped `config-defaults.json` sets `""`, and `syncConfigDefaults` overwrites the user's copy from the bundle on every launch, so a hand-edited value is gone after a restart — with a stock build, an overloaded gateway model ends the turn with a typed error and no fallback at all. Where an admin does bundle a value, two things are visible. First, a doc-shaped array (`"fallbackModel": ["a","b"]`) is silently coerced to `""` by `storage.ts:273-276`, so the admin sees no fallback and no error — the config looks accepted. Second, with a scalar value the single hop works once, and then the session keeps running on the fallback model for every later message: `retryWithFallbackModel` calls `setModel` and never restores the primary, while no event tells the renderer, so the model selector still shows the primary the user chose. A user who hits one transient gateway drain silently finishes the conversation on a different (usually weaker) model than the UI reports. A Claude-backed session gets no fallback at any setting.
